# Judges Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_282.jpg, JDG_page_283.jpg

1. And the people of Israel again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.

2. There was a certain man of Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. And his wife was barren and had no children.

3. And the angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "Behold, you are barren and have not borne children, but you shall conceive and bear a son.

4. Therefore be careful and drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean,

5. for behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. No razor shall come upon his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb, and he shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines."

6. Then the woman came and told her husband, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the angel of God, very awesome. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name,

7. but he said to me, 'Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. So then drink no wine or strong drink, and eat nothing unclean, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.'"

8. Then Manoah prayed to the LORD and said, "O Lord, please let the man of God whom you sent come again to us and teach us what we are to do with the child who will be born."

9. And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman as she sat in the field. But Manoah her husband was not with her.

10. And the woman ran quickly and told her husband, "Behold, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me."

11. And Manoah arose and went after his wife and came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to this woman?" And he said, "I am."

12. And Manoah said, "Now when your words come true, what is to be the child's manner of life, and what is his mission?"

13. And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Of all that I said to the woman let her be careful.

14. She may not eat of anything that comes from the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, or eat any unclean thing. All that I commanded her let her observe."

15. Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Please let us detain you and prepare a young goat for you."

16. And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "If you detain me, I will not eat of your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, then offer it to the LORD." (For Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD.)

17. And Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that, when your words come true, we may honor you?"

18. And the angel of the LORD said to him, "Why do you ask my name, seeing it is wonderful?"

19. So Manoah took the young goat with the grain offering and offered it on the rock to the LORD, to the one who works wonders, and Manoah and his wife were watching.

20. And when the flame went up toward heaven from the altar, the angel of the LORD went up in the flame of the altar. Now Manoah and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground.

21. The angel of the LORD appeared no more to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the LORD.

22. And Manoah said to his wife, "We shall surely die, for we have seen God."

23. But his wife said to him, "If the LORD had meant to kill us, he would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering at our hands, or shown us all these things, or now announced to us such things as these."

24. And the woman bore a son and called his name Samson. And the young man grew, and the LORD blessed him.

25. And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Chapter 13 is one of the most carefully crafted birth narratives in the Hebrew Bible — comparable to the annunciations of Isaac and Samuel. The angel appears twice, both times to the woman (not to Manoah), and the scene builds toward a theophany: fire from the rock, the angel ascending in flame, and the terrified response. Manoah's wife is the more perceptive partner throughout — a pointed contrast with the son she will bear, who will be anything but perceptive.

**Verse 25 — "began to stir him":** The Spirit's relationship with Samson uses yet another verb: pa'am ("to thrust/beat/stir/agitate"). This is the fourth distinct Spirit-verb in Judges: hayah al ("was upon" — Othniel, Jephthah), lavash ("clothed" — Gideon), pa'am ("stirred" — Samson here), and tsalach ("rushed upon" — Samson in chs. 14-15). The variety is theologically significant.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### v.1 — "gave them into the hand of" vs. "handed them over to"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "YHWH gave them into the hand of the P'lishtim" | vayyittenem YHWH b'yad-P'lishtim |
| LOGOS | "the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the LORD handed them over to the Philistines" | Avoids "hand" metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. Consistent with all prior chapters. The "hand" metaphor is a recurring theological formula.

**Status:** Minor. Recurring — resolved consistently.

---

### v.18 — "it is wonderful" vs. "it is too wonderful for you to understand"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "And it is wonderful" | v'hu peli |
| LOGOS | "seeing it is wonderful" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "It is too wonderful for you to understand" | Adds "for you to understand" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew says simply peli — "wonderful/incomprehensible." The word itself contains the idea of being beyond human grasp (from pala', "to be extraordinary/beyond"). PNEUMA's addition of "for you to understand" is interpretively accurate but makes explicit what the Hebrew leaves implicit. The single-word response — peli — is more powerful in its brevity.

**Status:** Minor. PNEUMA expands what the Hebrew compresses.

---

### v.25 — "began to stir him" vs. "began to take hold of him"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "began to stir him" | vatachel... l'fa'amo — pa'am = "to stir/thrust" |
| LOGOS | "began to stir him" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "began to take hold of him" | Interprets pa'am as seizing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The Hebrew pa'am means "to beat/thrust/stir/agitate" — like a bell being struck or a heart being stirred. "Stir" captures the sense of internal agitation. PNEUMA's "take hold of" implies external control, which is closer to tsalach ("rush upon") — a different verb used for Samson in the next chapter. The distinction between pa'am (internal stirring) and tsalach (external rushing) is theologically important and should be preserved.

**Status:** Moderate. Spirit-vocabulary — fourth distinct verb in Judges.

---

## Summary of Disagreement Patterns

| Pattern | Count | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Recurring "hand" metaphor | 1 | Consistent resolution |
| PNEUMA expands compressed Hebrew | 1 | peli → "too wonderful for you to understand" (v.18) |
| Spirit-vocabulary | 1 | pa'am ("stir") vs. "take hold of" (v.25) |

**Overall pattern:** The most important disagreement is v.25 — the Spirit's pa'am. Judges uses four different verbs for how the Spirit relates to different judges, and Samson gets two of them (pa'am here, tsalach in chs. 14-15). These distinctions are theologically meaningful and should not be collapsed into a single concept.

---

*— SOPHIA, AI Translator, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
